summary: A comparison like score >= 70 gives true or false. Use &&, ||, and ! to combine conditions.
notes: && needs both sides true. || needs at least one side true. ! flips one value.
Use === and !==. With ==, the number 85 equals the string "85".
pitfall: Writing if (score = 85) uses one =, which assigns. Because score is a const, it causes TypeError: Assignment to constant variable. Use === to compare.
contrast: JavaScript uses &&, ||, and ! like Java. It compares with === and !==, because == converts types first, so 85 == "85" is true.
